vocabulary.definition: In slang spoken English if we say something is a "sorry looking display" or just a "sorry display" it means that some kind of behavior is really poor and pathetic. Yesterday was the first time I played basketball in 2 years. It was a sorry display.

In spoken English, we often say "in" instead of "wearing" for certain types of clothes. I need to change if I want to go out. I'm still in my gym clothes. You look really good in that shirt. I'm super warm in this new winter coat.
This is short for "pajamas" which is a word for bedclothes or sleeping clothes.

If someone is "hooked" on something it means they are almost addicted to it and can't stop doing it. I'm hooked on this new TV show. I downloaded 2 seasons last night and watched all of it. It's really easy to get hooked on certain types of junk food.

vocabulary.term: It's a sad state of affairs
vocabulary.definition: If something is a "sad state of affairs" it means it's a weak and pathetic situation. I lost my job and have a lot of credit card debt. It's a pretty sad state of affairs. I need to do fix this fast.

In spoken English, if someone says, "I hear ya" it means they understand what you are experiencing and feeling because they have also been in that situation before or feel the same way about something. A: I hate getting up so early for work. It's the most annoying thing about my job. B: I hear ya.

If we don't know an exact number and want to say a number that is close we can say "or something". It's the same thing as "about" or "approximately". A: How much money did those shoes cost? B: 140 USD or something.

If someone is talking about "their prime" it means the time of their life they were at their best. This is used a lot in sports. In his prime, Michael Jordan was the best basketball player of all time. He used to be a really good football player but he's past his prime. He's still not bad but he's a lot slower than the younger players.
